title: DO NOT FEAR — I HAVE GIVEN THEM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them; I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to withstand you." After an all-night march from Gilgal, Joshua took them by surprise. The Lord threw them into confusion before Israel, so Joshua and the Israelites defeated them completely at Gibeon. — Josh 10:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the battle, God speaks the words Joshua most needed to hear: "Do not be afraid of them; I have given them into your hand." Once again God speaks of the victory in the past tense, as already accomplished. Facing five kings and their combined armies, Joshua could rest not on his own strength but on God's finished promise.

Then notice how the victory came. Joshua and his men did their part — an exhausting all-night march to take the enemy by surprise. But the decisive factor was this: "The Lord threw them into confusion before Israel." The real battle was won by God, who scattered the enemy in panic. Human effort and divine power worked together, but the credit clearly belonged to the Lord.

This is a wonderful pattern for the life of faith. We are called to obey and to labour — to make the "all-night march" of faithful effort. Yet we never trust in our own marching. We trust in the God who goes before us and does what we could never do ourselves. Our part is obedience; God's part is the victory.

The command "do not be afraid" runs like a thread through Scripture, always anchored in God's presence and promise, not in favourable circumstances. Joshua's enemies were real and strong. His confidence came from God's word alone. For us in Christ, the same assurance holds: "If God is for us, who can be against us?" (Rom 8:31). We labour faithfully, but we rest in a victory God Himself secures.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you draw your courage from your circumstances, or from God's promises?
2. How can you hold together faithful effort and full trust in God's power?
3. What fear do you need to bring under the truth that God has already secured the victory?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me not to fear my enemies but to trust Your promise. I will do my part in faithful effort, but I rest in You alone to give the victory. Amen.
